rationale: ary3 is a tiny (512-byte text, 2-function) Shootout kernel whose main function consists of extremely hot array-iteration loops, so the table prioritizes passes with low steady-state runtime overhead: SUB gets the highest weights because instruction substitution yields solid security/diversity gains with negligible runtime, size, and correctness cost; IGV is favored next since ary3's behavior is dominated by array/global data access patterns that global-variable indirection hides cheaply; SPLIT and BCF receive moderate security/diversity weights with suppressed RuntimeCost so they are applied conservatively where block structure benefits without bloating the hot loop; FLA keeps a decent security gain but its RuntimeCost weight is kept low because flattening dispatch loops inside ary3's inner iterations would be the single largest performance risk; IBR and ICALL get mid-range security weights with low RuntimeCost and elevated CorrectnessRisk (0.3/0.2) reflecting that indirect branches/calls in this minimal-call program add overhead and mis-compilation risk disproportionate to their benefit, so they are only selected for functions whose features strongly justify them. Overall, high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights across all passes preserve reverse-engineering resistance, while uniformly low RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights keep the scheduler from applying expensive transformations to this runtime-critical, size-minimal kernel.
